描述_ZN: There are ten stone drums, made of granite, about 90 cm high and 60 cm in diameter.　　The stone drums are named after the drum-shaped stone on which the text is carved in seal script. The stone is engraved with ten poems describing the hunting trips in big seal script, so it is also called "Hunting Jie". The poems are all in four lines, which are similar to the poem "Che Tackle" in "Shi Jing Xiao Ya". It is the earliest surviving set of stone inscriptions in China. Since the Tang Dynasty, Wei Yingyi and Han Yu made the "Song of the Stone Drum" to express the chapter, and then it became a big phenomenon in the world. The age of the stone drum has been said to be Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn Period, Warring States, Qin Dynasty, Han Dynasty, Jin Dynasty, Northern Wei, Western Wei, Northern Zhou and so on. Later, after examination and research by jinshi scholars from various aspects such as its content, script and calligraphic style, it was identified as a relic of the Qin Dynasty. The exact date has not yet been agreed upon, but among those who claim that it is a relic of the Qin Dynasty, there are also sayings such as Duke Wen of Qin, Duke Mu of Qin, Duke Xiang of Qin, and Duke Xian of Qin.　　The stone drums were found in the early Tang Dynasty in Tianxing, Shaanxi Province (now Fengxiang, Shaanxi Province). After that, it was moved to Tokyo (now Kaifeng) in the Song Dynasty, and when the Jin Dynasty broke the Song Dynasty, it was moved to Yanjing (now Beijing). After several migrations, the text was much worn out and damaged. Tokyo was filled with gold, and then removed after transporting Yanjing. One of the drums has no characters.　　Some of the characters in the stone drum script are the same as those in the pre-Han script. It is also called the Great Seal Script, which is said to have been made by the Emperor Shih Zhou during the reign of King Xuan of Zhou. It was popular in the Qin Dynasty during the Spring and Autumn Period, and was further simplified and linearized in the process. The calligraphy of this stone drum script is so simple and ancient that Kang Youwei of the Qing Dynasty said, "It is like a gold inlay on the ground or a group of clouds of grass. The seal script of some calligraphers in the Qing dynasty was mostly based on this.　　The topos of the stone drum script in the Forbidden City include the topos of the early Ming Dynasty, which was collected by Sun Kehong in the Ming Dynasty and is a famous book in China.　　It was recorded in Li Jifu's "Yuanhe County Map" in Tang Dynasty, Ouyang Xiu's "Ji Gu Lu" in Song Dynasty, Zhao Mingcheng's "Jin Shi Lu" and Zheng Qiao's "Shi Gu Wen Kao".
